newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas follows OTC up in May, not traded later.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas follows OTC up in May, not traded later.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures contract traded only 60 lots in four separate deals on Monday, all in May at higher prices.
But in other months, bids and offers were wide apart or not posted at all on a quiet day when the first trade was only struck little over half an hour before the market closed.
The physical market had gone up in May, dealers said, and futures levels followed, although for a long time it was just the bid/offer levels which were tracking up.
Four deals were then done in a tight range of 10.625 pence to 10.65 pence a therm, and by the close the bid/offer spread was reasonably tight at 10.595/10.65 pence a therm.
Tuesday is the last day of trading on the May contract.
Further forward there were no bids or offers posted from December 1997 to April 1998, the last month of the contract.
Shortly before the contract closed, bids and offers were only posted in three separate months.
